arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Brunstad argued the court must deny abusive motions.
He cited Section 105 and inherent judicial power.
Ms. Blatt argued courts have inherent authority to sanction bad faith.
She stated courts must prevent abuse of process.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Marrama seeks to convert his Chapter 7 case to Chapter 13. He claims the lower court wrongly denied this request. Citizens Bank argues the denial was a valid sanction for his bad faith conduct.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Marrama wants the Supreme Court to reverse the denial of his conversion request.
Citizens Bank wants the Supreme Court to affirm the denial of his conversion request.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Marrama argues the bankruptcy court lacks inherent authority to deny conversion as a sanction.
Citizens Bank argues the court has inherent authority to deny conversion to prevent abuse.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of bankruptcy court power to sanction bad faith. It determines whether courts can deny relief to punish procedural abuse. This affects how debtors interact with the bankruptcy system.
